name: Baselines: is it foresight or just caution? Final filter vs matched-rate random intervention vs always-cautious
setting: as final test 2 (normal mass, 2x execution noise, HARD_OFF, per-episode seeds); all four arms of an episode in one cluster job

arms.cbfm: final filter (h_safe = log2 3), frozen as in final test 2
arms.cbfr: matched-rate random trigger: identical fix procedure (closest safe of 15 policy samples + 3 primitives, h_safe = log2 3), but the decisions to act on are chosen at random with probability 0.071 (the final filter's rate in final test 2), seeded per episode
arms.slow: always cautious: every chunk executes half of the policy's planned displacement (the filter's 'half speed' move), no monitor

primary: foresight: cbfm vs cbfr, one-sided exact McNemar on neighbour topples (cbfm avoids vs cbfm suffers). Supported if p < 0.05.
secondary: cbfm vs slow: topples (McNemar) and success (cbfm >= slow is the expectation). cbfr and slow vs record reported.
reporting: All four arms, all comparisons, intervention counts, whatever the outcome; these numbers are a reported baseline result.
